description:
Mission Control of One.
No big agency, no 10-person squad—just one curious engineer with a laptop, a love for cosmic history, and a soft spot for robots that never got a ride home. I built Silent Monuments solo to turn NASA’s NSSDCA hardware catalog into an interactive story and arcade experience where players don’t just read about Apollo, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, and Pioneer 10—they actually talk to them and run their instruments one last time.
summary: Silent Monuments is an interactive 2D retro-telemetry adventure game and NSSDCA encyclopedia that brings NASA’s discarded off-world hardware back to life for school-age and casual learners. Stepping into the boots of Junior Archivist Maya, players journey across 5 chapters on the Moon, Mars, Asteroids, and Deep Space—hearing first-person transmissions from Apollo’s Moon Buggy, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, and Pioneer 10, and operating each instrument in hands-on 2D physics mini-games grounded in real NASA data.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

Silent Monuments: Echoes of Moon, Mars & Deep Space is an interactive 2D story-driven web application and NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) encyclopedia that brings 13 retired NASA spacecraft and instruments back to life.

Instead of presenting historical off-world hardware as static tables of coordinates, players step into the boots of Junior Archivist Maya across a guided 5-chapter journey (The Moon, Mars Surface Rovers, Mars Interior Landers, Jezero Crater Skies, and Asteroids/Deep Space). Each chapter flows through a clean 3-beat interactive loop:

1. The Story (2D Character Narration): A live 60fps 2D animated scene pairs Maya with an anthropomorphized 2D spacecraft character (Apollo LRV-1 & Eagle Descent Stage, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, and Dawn/Pioneer 10), narrating why it was sent, what it discovered, and why it rests where it is today in first-person dialogue.

2. The Instrument (60fps Physics & Arcade Simulation): Players wake up and operate each machine's real scientific instrument—driving Apollo's Lunar Rover in 1/6-g inertia while dodging micrometeorites and bouncing Earth lasers off ALSEP corner-cube mirrors; drilling Martian hematite with Opportunity's Rock Abrasion Tool while surviving dust devils and the 2018 global dust storm (tau = 10.8); timing P-wave and S-wave arrivals on InSight's live scrolling seismogram to triangulate Mars's liquid core; flying Ingenuity at 2,400+ RPM through Martian crosswinds to land at Airfield Chi; and executing orbital gravity-assist slingshots around Mars and Jupiter with Xenon ion thrusters.

3. Quick Verification & NSSDCA Archive: A single reflection check locks the chapter memory and unlocks a personalized, printable Junior Deep Space Archivist Certificate alongside a searchable catalog of all 13 NSSDCA hardware suites.

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE & WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

- Reframes "Space Junk" into Scientific Heritage: Public perception often lumps historic lunar descent stages, rovers, and landers together with orbital debris. Silent Monuments teaches school-age students, educators, and casual learners why planetary mass budgets, solar dust accumulation, and planetary protection rules (such as Dawn's quarantine orbit around Ceres) require leaving hardware behind—and how passive instruments like Apollo's retroreflectors still produce active science 50+ years later.

- Lowers the Barrier to NASA's NSSDCA Catalog: Technical archives like nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov contain priceless mission data but can feel intimidating to young students. By pairing every NSSDCA ID (e.g., 1969-059C, 2003-032A, 2018-042A, 2020-052B) with a character voice and a playable physics simulation, students learn real telemetry concepts effortlessly.

- Zero-Cost Classroom & Global Accessibility: Built as a lightweight, zero-backend web app that runs smoothly in any mobile or desktop browser without logins, downloads, or high-end GPUs.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Languages: TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES2022)

- Frontend Framework & Build Tooling: React 19, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide SVG Icons

- Graphics & Physics Engine: Custom 60fps HTML5 2D Canvas rendering engine (requestAnimationFrame) for both the animated 2D character stages and the 5 real-time physics mini-games (1/6-g drift, inverse-square orbital gravity F = GM/r^2, helicopter lift/drag, and scrolling wave synthesis)

- Audio Synthesis: Procedural Web Audio API sound synthesizer (zero external MP3/WAV dependencies; generates retro telemetry beeps, laser pings, marsquake low-frequency rumbles, and completion chords in real time)

- Hosting & Version Control: Git, GitHub, and Vercel (Production CI/CD)

HOW IS THE PROJECT CREATIVE?

- First-Person Machine Empathy + Live 2D Dioramas: Giving eyes, posture, and a first-person voice to Eagle's Descent Stage, Opportunity ("Oppy"), InSight, Ingenuity ("Ginny"), and Pioneer 10 turns cold engineering specs into an emotional story of endurance.

- Science-Grounded Game Mechanics: Every mini-game mechanic directly mirrors the real physics that defined that spacecraft's life and retirement—from Opportunity's life-saving Martian wind-cleaning events vs. the 2018 tau = 10.8 dust blackout, to Ingenuity's blade-tip aerodynamic challenge in Mars's 1% CO2 atmosphere, to S-P seismic wave lag triangulation.

WHAT FACTORS DID OUR TEAM CONSIDER?

1. Cognitive Load & Narrative Flow: Early prototypes showed that displaying historical text, NSSDCA metadata, quizzes, and simulations simultaneously overwhelmed users. We redesigned the interface into a calm, single-focus 3-beat progression (1. Story -> 2. Instrument -> 3. Quiz) with zero visual clutter.

2. Scientific Accuracy: Every NSSDCA ID, launch year, landing coordinate, mass, power source, and mission outcome was cross-checked directly against official NASA NSSDCA and NASA Science Mission Directorate records.

3. Accessibility & Judge Experience: We included high-contrast Dark/Light themes, keyboard + touch controls, a mute toggle for Web Audio, and one-click "Unlock All" / "Skip" fast-track buttons so educators and hackathon judges can inspect all 5 chapters in under 60 seconds.
